title: Yellow rainfall warning up in Metro Manila, 5 areas in Luzon
summary: MANILA, Philippines — The state weather bureau placed Metro Manila and five other areas in Luzon under a yellow rainfall warning on Wednesday due to the effects of the southwest monsoon or habagat.…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The state weather bureau placed Metro Manila and five other areas in Luzon under a yellow rainfall warning on Wednesday due to the effects of the southwest monsoon or habagat.

In its Heavy Rainfall Warning No. 18 issued at 11 a.m., the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa) said the following areas were under the yellow warning level:

items: Metro Manila: Caloocan, Malabon, Navotas, Valenzuela, Quezon City, Makati, Mandaluyong, San Juan, Pasay, Marikina, and Manila
Zambales: Olongapo, Subic, Castillejos, San Marcelino, San Narciso, San Antonio, Iba, Botolan, Cabangan, Palauig, San Felipe, Masinloc, and Candelaria

blocks.text: Areas under yellow warning tend to experience rainfall between 7.5 mm and 15 mm within one hour and can continue in the next two hours.
The yellow warning level likewise indicates a need for the public to “be alert,” with flooding in flood-prone areas identified as its associated hazard, Pagasa said.
Several local government units have already suspended in-person afternoon classes this Wednesday due to the forecast rains.
Meanwhile, according to Pagasa, light to moderate rains with occasional heavy rains were expected within the next three hours over Laguna, portions of Rizal, Bulacan, Tarlac, Batangas, and Quezon.
The same rainfall conditions were affecting portions of Nueva Ecija, Zambales, Pampanga, Cavite and Metro Manila, which may persist within three hours and could affect nearby areas.
Pagasa will release its next rainfall warning at 2 p.m. /jpv
